questions.questionText: Why are independent freelancers particularly attractive targets for social engineering scams?

options.text: They possess administrative access to enterprise military networks.
They operate without corporate IT security perimeters and face financial pressure to secure new client contracts.
Freelancers are legally required to accept all incoming client files.
Freelancing platforms block all security software.

questions.explanation: Income unpredictability and isolation from corporate IT oversight increase vulnerability to fake client lures (Ticona, 2022).

questions.questionText: A client demanding that you log into a third-party website using your personal Google or Microsoft credentials to view a project brief is a major indicator of portfolio credential harvesting.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Legitimate project briefs do not require logging in with personal OAuth credentials on unverified third-party domains.

questions.questionText: A prospective client offers you a $5,000 project but insists on moving communications off Upwork to Telegram before a contract is started. They offer to pay via an unverified check. What should you do?

options.text: Move to Telegram immediately to secure the contract.
Decline to move off-platform and insist on using platform-based contracts and escrow funding.
Send the client your banking account password so they can deposit the funds directly.
Accept the check and send completed work before the check clears.

questions.explanation: Luring freelancers off-platform removes contract enforcement and escrow protections, exposing them to payment fraud.

questions.questionText: Which of the following indicate that an incoming freelance inquiry is a social engineering scam? (Select TWO)

options.text: The client provides a clear project scope and agrees to use platform escrow.
The client sends an advance payment check exceeding the project price and requests an immediate wire refund of the difference.
The client demands your staging server login credentials before signing a contract or funding escrow.
The client verified their payment method on a recognized freelancing platform.

questions.explanation: Overpayment refund demands and premature requests for administrative server credentials are key fraud indicators.

questions.questionText: Escrow services on freelance platforms protect freelancers by holding client funds in a neutral account until agreed project milestones are met.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Escrow ensures funds are verified and set aside before work begins, reducing non-payment risks.

questions.questionText: What is the primary objective of a "Portfolio Credential Harvesting" attack targeting freelancers?

options.text: To optimize the freelancer's search engine ranking.
To steal the freelancer's primary account passwords, cloud storage logins, or platform access tokens.
To automatically update the freelancer's operating system.
To pay the freelancer in advance.

questions.explanation: Fake login portals capture credentials to compromise professional accounts and cloud repositories.

questions.questionText: You receive a $2,000 advance payment check from a new client. Two days later, the client emails: "Our accountant made a mistake and sent $3,500. Please Zelle us back the $1,500 difference right away." What is the safest course of action?

options.text: Send the $1,500 via Zelle immediately to maintain good client relations.
Do not send any funds; alert your bank that the check is likely fraudulent and wait for it to fully clear or bounce.
Send $750 as a compromise.
Cash the check at a grocery store.

questions.explanation: Fake check overpayment scams rely on the victim wiring real money before the bank discovers the deposited check is counterfeit.

questions.questionText: Which domain name represents a typosquatted domain designed to trick a freelancer using Figma for client design reviews?

options.text: figma.com/file/12345/project
figma-verify-review.net/login
help.figma.com
community.figma.com

questions.explanation: Adding words like -verify-review.net creates a lookalike domain to capture OAuth credentials.

questions.questionText: Legitimate corporate clients will routinely ask freelancers to purchase gift cards as part of their initial onboarding duties.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Requesting gift card purchases during onboarding is a classic financial scam.

questions.questionText: What should a freelancer do before opening a zip file sent by a new, unverified client?

options.text: Open the zip file immediately on a production server.
Inspect the file extension, run an antivirus scan, and verify the client's identity through independent channels.
Forward the file to all contacts in their address book.
Rename the file extension to .exe.

questions.explanation: Unverified attachments can contain malicious scripts or executable payloads.
